executive_summary.headline: Strait of Hormuz transit collapse and elevated energy costs are driving AMBER world risk despite supplier and peer signals stabilizing.
executive_summary.next_step: Within 48 hours, model the exposure of your top 20 suppliers to energy price shocks and shipping-route dependencies, then flag any whose margins or working capital may be at risk if current crude and gas prices persist.
executive_summary.context: Hormuz transits have plunged 96% year-on-year as of 25 October, while Brent crude stands 30% above its one-year median and EU natural gas is 131% above September 2025 levels. Rhine water levels remain below operational thresholds at both Maxau and Kaub. Separately, two high-exposure semiconductor and contract-manufacturing suppliers posted unexplained single-day drops (Infineon −6.0%, Jabil −6.6%) on 22 October with no corroborating news; whether these are connected to energy or shipping stress…
